topic: Closed-form sharp multi-regime effect bounds for a two-source binary collider SCM. Let X,Z,Y be binary in the recursive graph X→Y←Z with two mutually independent latent roots shared along X↔Y and Z↔Y and independent private outcome noise. Given normalized strictly positive tables A(x,y)=P(X=x,Y=y | do(Z=0)) and B(z,y)=P(Z=z,Y=y | do(X=0)), set p=A(0,0)+A(0,1), r=B(0,0)+B(0,1), a=A(0,1), and b=B(0,1). Prove compatibility iff -(1-p)r≤a-b≤p(1-r), and prove that q=P(Y=1 | do(X=0,Z=0)) has the sharp interval [max{a,b,a+b-pr}, min{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)}]. Construct source-preserving finite SCMs attaining every real interval point and rational endpoint certificates for rational inputs. Give the constant-time compatibility/endpoint procedure and an optional simultaneous-multinomial outer confidence interval, while excluding any general thicket compiler or field-tier claim. Credit Duarte et al., JASA 2024, Autobounds as the same-input generic polynomial-program comparator and Zaffalon et al., IJAR 2023, as adjacent multi-source approximate bounding work; Autobounds is the software consumer whose generic optimization would be replaced by this analytic certificate. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Independent derivation parameterized the fiber by c and d, obtaining q=a+b-c+d, and built one finite private-threshold law matching all eight table cells. Exact checks matched 1,225 positive denominator-eight table pairs to LP values, including 42 pinned-c cases, and reconstructed 3,339 finite SCMs; the positive witness yields [1/8,1/2], and a correlated-source control escapes the valid independent-source bound. Current primary-source searches found generic methods but no exact formula collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the universal source-preserving threshold extension in Section 4: one finite private-noise law and one deterministic outcome function must reproduce every prescribed response and both complete experimental tables. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct both endpoint SCMs for A=((1/8,3/8),(3/8,1/8)) and B=((3/8,1/8),(3/8,1/8)); require exact agreement with all eight cells, mutually independent roots, and target values 3/8 and 5/8. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_binary_ctf_thicket_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can every compatible pair of strictly positive binary-collider regime tables and every target value in the claimed sharp interval be realized by one finite SCM with mutually independent shared roots, one private outcome noise, and one deterministic outcome function?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic canonical-SCM programs verify feasibility only after optimizing over a large response-function representation, while separate realizations of the two experimental margins do not establish a common extension. The missing proof step is to couple all prescribed response blocks into one deterministic outcome map while preserving the product law of the two shared roots and the private outcome noise. Prior CausalSmith reviews explicitly warn that armwise completions cannot be pasted, and the web scan found no primary source giving the claimed compatibility inequality, max/min endpoint formula, or universal finite extension.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive characterization that either supplies bounded finite latent supports and explicit source-preserving weights for every feasible target value, including exact endpoint reconstructions for the stated denominator-eight kill test, or gives a compatible table pair and interval point refuting universal extension.

writing_exemplar.why: Its compatibility–ambiguity–falsifiability framing is the closest motivation arc for overlapping causal reports that must arise from one SCM.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Separate experiments reveal overlapping causal margins -> counterfactual consistency restricts their common SCM -> hidden independent sources create nonlinear compatibility -> obtain an exact interval and one source-preserving realization for every point

method_exemplars.technique: Canonical response-function polynomialization and extraction of feasible endpoint witnesses from the discrete SCM program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the same-input generic optimization whose product-source constraints must be eliminated analytically.

method_exemplars.technique: Response-function reduction followed by primal-dual symbolic analysis and explicit tightness witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired max/min expressions are symbolic extrema over finite response types, augmented here by independent-source product restrictions.

method_exemplars.technique: Influence-function estimation and limit theory for nonsmooth sharp-bound functionals, using margin conditions or smooth approximations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The claimed collider endpoints are finite maxima and minima of multinomial-cell functionals.

open_problems.open_problem: Can compatibility and the piecewise-affine sharp interval be equipped with asymptotically exact simultaneous inference that remains uniformly valid at feasibility boundaries and ties among endpoint formulas?

source_refs.claim: The ordinary bootstrap generally fails for directionally differentiable maps such as maxima and minima at nondifferentiability points.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang, Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Inference for nonsmooth sharp causal bounds requires margin conditions or regularized approximations, which do not directly settle uniform behavior along tie sequences.
source_refs.author: Alexander W. Levis, Matteo Bonvini, Zhenghao Zeng, Luke Keele, Edward H. Kennedy
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.excerpt: A proof of uniform tie-inclusive coverage and uniform level ... is still absent.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Compatibility is an inequality-defined null with a changing active face, while each bound endpoint is a maximum or minimum of affine functions of two multinomial probability vectors. At equality or a tie, ordinary differentiability fails, estimated fibers may become spuriously empty, and a bootstrap calibrated for one selected formula need not cover the entire identified interval. Existing generic projection methods are conservative, and available smooth or margin-condition arguments exclude or regularize the difficult local sequences.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A compatibility test and simultaneous confidence interval for the complete sharp set with a stated local asymptotic law, uniform level and coverage over positive tables including ties, and explicit behavior under root-n local approaches to or violations of the compatibility boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates population sharpness from sampling uncertainty and directly motivates improving conservative optimization-based confidence bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Population tables determine sharp causal bounds -> experiments reveal tables only through samples -> generic table-region projection is conservative -> exploit the closed-form collider geometry for tie-robust nominal inference

method_exemplars.technique: Directional delta method with an estimated directional derivative and modified bootstrap for nondifferentiable maps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite max/min endpoint maps are canonical Hadamard directionally differentiable functionals whose nondifferentiability occurs exactly at ties.

method_exemplars.technique: Studentized moment-inequality relaxation and bootstrap calibration targeted at a projected functional, with uniform-coverage analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The compatibility restriction and bound faces form a low-dimensional moment-inequality model whose projection is the causal interval.

method_exemplars.technique: Efficient estimation of maxima and minima defining sharp causal bounds under margin conditions, plus regularized alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the nearest causal-bound limit theory and identifies what changes when active endpoint formulas tie.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the compatibility conditions and attained sharp target interval when the two binary-collider experimental tables may contain structural zeros rather than being strictly positive?

source_refs.excerpt: The row-span iff fails on a boundary compatibility fiber.
first-forbidden-prefix saturation yields the unique maximal Cartesian response support

open_problems.why_unsolved: Strict positivity holds the active response support fixed. A zero cell forces response types to disappear, can lower the affine dimension of the fiber, and can turn formerly redundant inequalities into identifying equalities. Consequently the interior fiber parameterization cannot simply be evaluated on the boundary: its first proof step must be replaced by a support-mask-specific active-face calculation before endpoint attainment can be established.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A support-stratified finite catalogue of necessary-and-sufficient compatibility conditions and attained target intervals, including same-support finite endpoint SCMs and rational certificates for rational boundary tables.

writing_exemplar.why: Its discrete-SCM optimization setup supplies the generic baseline against which active support faces can be presented as an analytically solvable special geometry.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Generic discrete bounds are polynomial programs -> structural zeros delete feasible response types -> the active compatibility face changes -> classify boundary fibers and their exact endpoint witnesses

method_exemplars.technique: Canonical finite response-type reduction restricted to response types surviving each observed support mask.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested formulas require characterizing the finite response carrier separately on each support face.

method_exemplars.technique: Exact algebraic feasibility analysis for small binary latent-variable causal structures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Boundary compatibility requires deciding which polynomial constraints become equalities on each lower-dimensional face.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrated projection inference for parameters constrained by moment equalities and inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A support-indexed compatibility system naturally becomes a changing collection of equality and inequality restrictions under sampling.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the simultaneous identified set of all four joint-intervention probabilities P(Y=1 | do(X=x,Z=z)) under the two observed regime tables, rather than four separately optimized coordinate intervals?

source_refs.claim: Generic polynomial programming can optimize declared discrete causal estimands individually but does not supply a symbolic description of their joint image.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Coordinatewise sharpness does not characterize the joint region because all four intervention responses must use the same deterministic outcome function and independent source roots. Generic solvers can optimize one linear projection at a time, but projection of the complete shared response-function fiber may produce cross-coordinate facets or nonlinear constraints invisible in marginal intervals. The first new proof step is therefore simultaneous elimination into four target coordinates.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit facet or semialgebraic description of the four-dimensional target set, a constant-time membership procedure for fixed binary domains, and a proof that every point is attained by one finite source-preserving SCM.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames how separately available causal margins can constrain yet fail to determine a shared common-effect mechanism.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Different experiments report different causal margins -> the reports must share one mechanism -> scalar bounds hide dependence among joint-intervention answers -> characterize the complete admissible response vector

method_exemplars.technique: Projection matrices mapping a common Boolean response-function representation to overlapping marginal causal models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired set is likewise the image of one shared response law under several target projections, with additional product-source constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Symbolic primal-dual elimination and redundancy removal for finite response-type models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Facet elimination, rather than repeated scalar optimization, is required for a simultaneous region.

method_exemplars.technique: Bootstrap-calibrated projection of moment-inequality confidence regions with uniform asymptotic coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite description of the joint target set would directly induce a projected confidence region for its coordinates and contrasts.

open_problems.open_problem: How do compatibility and sharp target bounds change when independence of the two shared collider roots is relaxed by a quantified dependence budget, and what is the smallest budget permitting escape from the independent-source interval?

open_problems.why_unsolved: At zero dependence the latent law factors, whereas unrestricted dependence gives a much larger coupling simplex. A total-variation, odds-ratio, or mutual-information budget produces an intermediate nonrectangular feasible set. The first source-method step that fails is factorization of latent-cell masses; it must be replaced by a sharp constrained-coupling characterization rather than an unrestricted response-signature relaxation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A budget-indexed compatibility criterion and attained piecewise-analytic target interval that recovers the independent-source result at zero, the unrestricted-coupling result at the maximal budget, and a certified first-escape threshold.

writing_exemplar.why: Its breakdown-frontier framing provides a disciplined narrative for quantifying how conclusions change as an identifying restriction is relaxed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact latent-source independence may be fragile -> a dependence budget grades departures from it -> sharp conclusions change along that path -> locate the first budget at which the collider bound breaks

method_exemplars.technique: Inflation-based compatibility inequalities that retain rather than erase independent latent-source structure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The opportunity concerns precisely the frontier between product-source compatibility and unrestricted latent coupling.

method_exemplars.technique: Response-function polynomial programs augmented by explicit constraints on latent joint masses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The budgeted interval is an endpoint problem over a constrained latent coupling fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Uniform inference for projections of models defined by changing moment-inequality contact sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Dependence budgets create a nested family of partially identified target sets with potentially changing active constraints.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A two-source fiber may collapse to a few scalar overlap variables, but a third independent root produces a multi-affine law over eight source cells and higher-order consistency constraints not detectable by pairwise table checks. The first proof step that changes is replacement of a two-way interval-intersection argument by elimination on a three-factor response object while retaining one shared deterministic outcome function and product-source realizability.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite inequality or equivalent compatibility description, an attained formula or polynomial-size recursion for the all-zero target interval, and finite rational endpoint SCMs for rational three-source inputs.

writing_exemplar.why: Its extensions discussion motivates merging more than two common-effect margins and identifies response-function growth as the central obstruction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Different studies reveal different cause–outcome margins -> all margins must arise from one common-effect mechanism -> an additional source tightens compatibility but explodes response types -> seek a scalable exact three-source characterization

method_exemplars.technique: Aggregate deterministic response functions into query-relevant hyperarcs and prove equivalence between the pruned and original bound programs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A three-source result must quotient the rapidly growing response-function set while preserving the observed regime tables and all-zero target.

method_exemplars.technique: Canonical discrete-SCM polynomial programming followed by symbolic projection to candidate compatibility facets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested characterization is the analytic projection of a finite source-factorized response program.

method_exemplars.technique: Uniformly calibrated projection inference for targets constrained by growing collections of moment inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any finite three-source compatibility description immediately produces a moment-inequality system for the causal endpoint.

literature_map:
Balke and Pearl (JASA 1997) are the foundational reference for closed-form sharp binary causal bounds obtained through response types and linear programming.
Tian and Pearl (AMAI 2000) combine observational and experimental information for probabilities of causation, but do not solve this independent-source collider query.
Shpitser and Pearl (JMLR 2008) characterize point identification across the causal hierarchy; the present target lies on the partial-identification side of that frontier.
Bareinboim and Pearl (UAI 2012) give complete graphical point-identification machinery for surrogate experiments, not sharp bounds when the fused target remains unidentified.
Finkelstein and Shpitser (UAI 2020) derive analytic bounds through cross-world logical implications, offering an alternative to exhaustive response-type enumeration.
Sachs, Jonzon, Sjölander, and Gabriel (JCGS 2022) automate symbolic tight bounds for linear response-function programs, whereas independent latent districts generally introduce product constraints.
Gresele et al. (ICML 2022, arXiv:2202.01300) are the closest formulation paper: overlapping common-effect SCMs, compatibility, and counterfactual ambiguity, with the main analytic case causally sufficient.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (ICML 2022, arXiv:2110.05690) establish canonical finite-SCM sufficiency for arbitrary experiment collections but use expensive polynomial programs and approximate search.
Zeitler and Silva (arXiv:2202.13851) use locally consistent causal marginals for tractability, explicitly sacrificing global independence information central here.
Duarte et al. (JASA 2024, arXiv:2109.13471) are the same-input generic comparator: Autobounds supplies polynomial optimization rather than a constant-time formula or rational witness certificate.
Zaffalon et al. (IJAR 2023, arXiv:2307.16577) fuse multiple observational and randomized sources through causal EM, but obtain approximate inner ranges rather than exact analytic bounds.
Shridharan and Iyengar (ICML 2023) prune discrete causal-bound programs and obtain selected closed forms, but not overlapping source-specific experiments with independent collider roots.
Wolfe, Spekkens, and Fritz (JCI 2019) and Navascués and Wolfe (JCI 2020) show that independent-source compatibility has genuinely nonlinear constraints and convergent inflation tests, explaining why unrestricted-latent reductions are unsafe.
For inference, Chernozhukov–Lee–Rosen (Econometrica 2013), Fang–Santos (ReStud 2019), Kaido–Molinari–Stoye (Econometrica 2019), and Levis et al. (JRSSB 2025) supply intersection-bound, directional-bootstrap, calibrated-projection, and nonsmooth-bound techniques.
No located primary source states the proposed binary-collider compatibility inequality, max/min interval, or universal source-preserving finite construction.
